sections.body: In music notation, a crotchet (quarter note) ♩ lasts 1 beat, a minim (half note) lasts 2 beats, and a semibreve (whole note) lasts 4 beats. Two quavers (eighth notes) ♫ share 1 beat.
Instrument families: STRINGS (violin, guitar, sitar), WOODWIND (flute, clarinet), BRASS (trumpet, trombone), PERCUSSION (drums, xylophone, tabla).
You can sort instruments by how they make sound: plucked or bowed strings, blowing air, or hitting.

quiz.q: How many beats does a minim (half note) last?
hints: A minim is twice as long.
A semibreve lasts 4 beats, which is double a minim. So a minim is half of 4.

quiz.q: A tabla is in which instrument family?
hints: How do you play a tabla?
You hit it with your hands.
Drums are hit to make sound. Which family are drums in?
quiz.explain: The tabla is played by hitting it, so it's percussion.

quiz.q: How many beats do two crotchets and one minim last altogether?
hints: Work out how long each note lasts, then add them up.
A crotchet lasts 1 beat. A minim is twice as long as a crotchet.
Example: two quavers and one minim. Two quavers share 1 beat, so 1 + 2 = 3 beats.
quiz.explain: Each crotchet lasts 1 beat and the minim lasts 2 beats. 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 beats.
